chain.title: Copper Chest
chain.desc: Copper ingots around a wooden chest; 45 slots, the first rung and the cheapest storage upgrade in the pack.

chain.title: Iron Chest
chain.desc: Iron ingots around a wooden chest, or glass and iron around a Copper Chest; 54 slots and the tier everything else is measured against.

chain.title: Gold Chest
chain.desc: Gold ingots around an Iron Chest; 81 slots in a nine-by-nine grid.

chain.title: Diamond Chest
chain.desc: Diamonds and glass around a Gold Chest; 108 slots, and the fork where the ladder splits two ways.

chain.title: Obsidian Chest
chain.desc: Obsidian around a Diamond Chest; 108 slots like the diamond tier, but blast-proof - the branch you take for a base you expect to be attacked.

chain.title: Crystal Chest
chain.desc: Glass around a Diamond Chest; 108 slots and a transparent shell that renders its contents, so you can read a wall of them at a glance.

chain.title: Wood to Copper Upgrade
chain.desc: Planks and copper ingots; right-click it onto a placed chest to convert it in the world, keeping every item already inside.

chain.title: Copper to Iron Upgrade
chain.desc: Copper, iron and glass; the upgrade path exists so you never have to empty a chest to promote it.

chain.title: Iron to Gold Upgrade
chain.desc: Iron and gold ingots in a frame; applied in place, it takes an Iron Chest to 81 slots without a single item moving.

chain.title: Gold to Diamond Upgrade
chain.desc: Gold, diamonds and glass; the most expensive rung of the upgrade line and the one that unlocks both endgame branches.

chain.title: Diamond to Obsidian Upgrade
chain.desc: Obsidian and glass; converts a placed Diamond Chest into the blast-proof variant on the spot.

chain.title: Diamond to Crystal Upgrade
chain.desc: The same obsidian-and-glass frame in a different arrangement; the other half of the diamond fork.

chain.title: Dirt Chest
chain.desc: Dirt, coarse dirt and podzol around a wooden chest. It has exactly one slot. It is a joke, it is craftable, and it is the only chest in the mod that is worse than the one you started with.

chain.title: Trapped Iron Chest
chain.desc: A tripwire hook plus any iron chest; every tier has a trapped twin that emits redstone when opened, and they upgrade along the same ladder.

notes: SHORT BY NATURE - this is a six-rung storage ladder with an upgrade item for each rung and a trapped twin for each chest, and that is the entire mod. 21 items, 21 quested across chain and wheels, nothing padded and nothing dropped. VERIFICATION: pass 1 strict models INTERSECT lang gave 21/21 with zero model-only, zero lang-only, zero blockstate-only ids - the cleanest jar in this batch. All 21 have crafting recipes, and all 14 chest blocks additionally have block loot tables so they survive being broken. Pass 2 re-derived the set independently from .class constant-pool strings, textures, blockstates, recipe results and loot tables: nothing unsupported, nothing missed. CONSENSUS CROSS-CHECK: moddb.json carries entries for this mod under BOTH 'ironchest' and 'ironchests' (two different mods share the chest-tier naming; only 'ironchest' is ProgWML6's Iron Chests, which is this jar). Its consensus order is copper -> iron -> gold -> diamond -> obsidian -> crystal. NO CONFLICT: the recipe graph gives exactly that order for the first four rungs, and obsidian and crystal are genuine siblings - both are crafted from a Diamond Chest, neither from the other - so consensus placing obsidian at 0.8 and crystal at 1.0 is consistent with the graph rather than contradicting it. The chain follows the graph and preserves the consensus tie-break. NOTE ON CAPACITY: obsidian and crystal hold the same 108 slots as diamond; they are lateral, not vertical, which is why the chain describes what each one buys you rather than pretending crystal is bigger. Jar confirmed 1.20.1 Forge: META-INF/mods.toml, modId ironchest, minecraft versionRange [1.20.1,1.21), pack_format 15, Java 17 class files, no fabric.mod.json.
